newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's property tax revenues rise in April.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's property tax revenues rise in April.

text.p: Lebanese government revenues from taxation of property deals rose 18.26 percent in April over the same month last year, the finance ministry said on Wednesday.
The ministry collected $10,134,274 compared with $8,570,099 in April 1996. It collected $13,325,928 last month, the ministry said in a statement.
Collected revenues for the first four months of 1997 totalled $42,840,508 compared with $36,795,030 over the same period a year earlier -- a rise of 16.43 percent.

Tax rates on property deals vary from district to district, but average about 6.5 percent. However, tax collection does not truly reflect the state of the market because deals are sometimes understated to avoid tax, property analysts say.
